speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have your symptoms been present, and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI).

Given your history of recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia and the onset of severe, watery diarrhea with cramping, I suspect this is a superimposed C. diff infection. I need to confirm this with a stool test; please have your nurse obtain a stool sample for a C. difficile toxin assay and a C. diff PCR panel.
